body: # 1800 GOT JUNK Louisville Kentucky Prices ## Introduction – What You’ll Learn If you’ve typed “1800 GOT JUNK Louisville Kentucky prices” into Google, you’re probably staring at a pile of unwanted furniture, old appliances, or construction debris and wondering how much it will cost to make it disappear. This guide breaks down the **exact pricing structure** of 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? in the Louisville market, shows you real‑life cost scenarios, compares the service to local competitors, and reveals hidden fees most people overlook. By the end, you’ll know **exactly what to expect on your invoice**, how to **avoid surprise charges**, and what steps you can take to **save money** without compromising on speed or professionalism. --- ## 1. How 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? Pricing Works in Louisville ### 1.1 The “Load‑Based” Model Explained 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? does not charge by the hour or by the square foot. Instead, the company uses a **load‑based pricing system** that is calibrated to the volume of junk you need removed. In Louisville, a “load” typically represents **up to 1/3 of a 12‑yard truck** (about 4 cubic yards). - **One Load** – $99 (standard price for residential customers) - **Two Loads** – $199 (10% discount on the second load) - **Three Loads** – $299 (further 10% discount) - **Four Loads** – $399 (maximum discount tier) If you exceed the volume of a single load, the driver will **automatically add a second load** and adjust the price accordingly. The pricing is **transparent**: the driver measures the load on the spot, and you get a final price before they lift a single item. ### 1.2 What’s Included in the Base Price? - **Labor** – All loading, lifting, and placement onto the truck. - **Transportation** – Delivery of the truck to your address and disposal at an authorized landfill or recycling facility. - **Disposal Fees** – Covered in the base price for most common waste streams (household junk, old appliances, mattresses, etc.). ### 1.3 Items That May Trigger Extra Fees | Item Type | Why It Costs More | Typical Extra Charge (Louisville) | |-----------|-------------------|-----------------------------------| | **Hazardous Materials** (paint, chemicals) | Requires special handling & EPA‑approved disposal | $25‑$75 per item | | **Large Appliances** (refrigerator, commercial freezer) | Needs extra labor & possibly a larger truck | $15‑$30 per appliance | | **Construction Debris** (concrete, brick) | Heavier, may exceed weight limits | $35‑$50 per load | | **Electronic Waste** (TVs, monitors) | Requires certified e‑waste recycling | $10‑$20 per item | The **key takeaway**: most everyday junk (couches, mattresses, boxes, yard waste) stays within the base price. Only **specialty items** push the cost upward. > **Pro Tip:** When you call for a quote, ask the dispatcher to **pre‑screen** any “special” items. A clear list helps avoid surprise fees when the truck arrives. --- ## 2. Items: 8 office chairs, 4 desks, 2 filing cabinets, a broken printer, and a small conference table. - **Estimated Volume:** 4.5 cubic yards (≈ 1.5 loads) - **Base Price:** $149 (one load + half‑load discount) - **Electronic Waste Fee:** $30 (printer) **Total Cost:** **$179**. ### 2.4 Example 4: Full‑Truck Load – Whole‑House Clear‑Out **Scenario:** An estate sale in the suburbs of Louisville.
